messages:
marta.support: FYI — ACME prod seeing SSL handshake aborted when routing to our Private endpoint through their corporate proxy/appliance. Errors from our side: 'SSL handshake failure (alert 40)'. Any known issues with proxies doing NTLM/TLS re-negotiation?
sre-aaron: Can you paste the curl/openssl output and the client stack? Also, is this happening only for TLS1.3 or all traffic?
marta.support: Repro snippet and s_client output below:
```
# curl used by customer
curl -v https://api.private.redwood.internal/v1/generate \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>"
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS header, Certificate Status (22):
* SSL connection using unknown
* fatal: TLS handshake failure
```
openssl s_client -connect api.private.redwood:443 -tlsextdebug -showcerts
# output ends with 'handshake failure' and alert 40
```
eng-maya: From the traces it looks like the appliance is inserting an NTLM challenge and trying to renegotiate the TLS session mid-handshake. Many middleboxes that do TLS inspection will terminate and re-initiate TLS (or force a rehandshake). Our runtime/client doesn't handle server-initiated renegotiation well in that path.
jamie.ops: Quick repro note: hit a corp proxy locally that returns 407 + NTLM then does a TLS rehandshake. OkHttp + JDK11 prefers TLS1.3; the proxy fails the resumed handoff. Workaround that worked locally: force TLSv1.2 on the client or bypass inspection.
marta.support: Customer says their appliance is 'SecureInspect v4', they have a policy 'strict-inspect' enabled which forces re-handshake and strips SNI for inspected hosts. They asked what exact TLS profile/ciphers we need so they can create an exception.
eng-maya: We officially support TLS1.2+ and TLS1.3. Recommended cipher suites to allow: AES_128_GCM, AES_256_GCM, CHACHA20_POLY1305, ECDHE key exchange with RSA/ECDSA certs. If they can't support TLS1.3, TLS1.2 with ECDHE_RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 is a good stable choice. Best long-term fix: bypass inspection for api.private.redwood or disable server-initiated renegotiation on appliance.
marta.support: Sent customer suggested settings and asked for tcpdump/pcap from their gateway. Also requested appliance logs for NTLM/inspect decisions. @sre-aaron can we add a temporary allowlist for the customer's egress IPs so they can test bypass?
sre-aaron: On it — added temporary rule to allow connections from 198.51.100.0/24 to our Private LB without TLS inspection. Also added an alert for handshake_failure spikes. Suggested debug command we asked them to run:
```
openssl s_client -connect api.private.redwood:443 -tls1_2 -cipher 'ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256' -servername api.private.redwood
```
proxy-gw-bot: Ticket #12345 updated: customer applied bypass on 2026-04-07; monitoring shows handshakes returning to normal :white_check_mark:
acme-netops: Confirmed — bypass applied on our appliance, calls to /v1/generate are returning 200s again. Thanks for the quick turnaround!
marta.support: Closing loop with customer, keeping SRE alert for 72h to watch for regressions.
